target: Yağmur yağarken dışarı çıkmak istemedim.
english: When it was raining, I didn't want to go outside.
tip: 'yağarken' means while it rains. Adding '-ken' to the aorist 'yağar' builds a while-doing clause running alongside the main action.

target: Babanın arabası çok eski ama sağlam.
english: Father's car is very old but solid.
tip: 'babanın arabası' means father's car. The owner takes '-nın' and the thing owned takes '-sı', so both ends of the pair are marked.

target: Ya otobüse bineriz ya da yürürüz.
english: Either we take the bus or we walk.
tip: 'ya otobüse bineriz ya da yürürüz' means either we take the bus or we walk. The frame 'ya ... ya da' sets up the two choices.

target: Gelecek ay tüm borçlarımı ödemiş olacağım.
english: By next month I will have paid all my debts.
tip: 'ödemiş olacağım' means I will have paid. The '-mış' form plus 'olacağım' places the action as finished by a future point.

target: Komşu bize su kesintisi olacağını haber verdi.
english: The neighbor informed us that there would be a water outage.
tip: 'olacağını' means that there will be, as the object of 'haber verdi'. The '-acağını' ending packs a whole future clause into one word ending in the object marker.

target: Kurduğumuz şirket büyümeye devam ediyor.
english: The company we founded continues to grow.
tip: 'büyümeye devam ediyor' means keeps growing. 'devam etmek' needs the '-e' ending on the verbal noun, so 'büyüme' becomes 'büyümeye'.

target: Annem bana mont giymemi söyledi.
english: My mother told me to wear a coat.
tip: To report a command, add '-me' plus a possessive and '-i' to the verb: 'giymemi söyledi' means told me to wear.

target: Araba köprünün üstünden geçerken manzara harika.
english: When the car passes over the bridge the view is amazing.
tip: Add '-ken' to a verb to mean while doing it: 'geçerken' means while passing.

target: İlk defa uçağa bindim, çok heyecanlandım.
english: I got on a plane for the first time, I was very excited.
tip: 'binmek' takes the '-a' ending for what you board: 'uçağa bindim' means I got on the plane.

target: Havalimanında gözyaşlarıyla vedalaştık.
english: We said goodbye at the airport with tears.
tip: The '-ş' in 'vedalaştık' marks a mutual action: we said goodbye to each other, not one-way.

target: Okulun bahçesi çok büyük.
english: The school's garden is very big.
tip: Possession takes two endings, '-un' on the owner and '-si' on the thing: 'okulun bahçesi' means the school's garden.

target: Bana söyleseydin yardım ederdim.
english: If you had told me, I would have helped.
tip: '-seydin' plus '-erdim' makes an unreal past: 'söyleseydin yardım ederdim' means if you had told me, I would have helped.

target: Çocuğun oyuncakları her yere dağılmış.
english: The child's toys are scattered everywhere.
tip: The '-miş' in 'dağılmış' shows an inferred result: the toys are scattered, noticed after the fact, not watched happening.

target: Çocukluk günlerimi anımsadığımda gözlerim doluyor.
english: My eyes fill with tears when I remember my childhood days.
tip: For when I do something, add '-dığım' plus '-da' to the verb: 'anımsadığımda' means when I remember.

target: Türkçe öğreniyorum, lütfen yavaş konuşur musunuz?
english: I'm learning Turkish, could you please speak slowly?
tip: The aorist plus 'mu' makes a polite request: 'konuşur musunuz' means would you please speak.

target: Bu dil dünyanın birçok ülkesinde konuşulur.
english: This language is spoken in many countries of the world.
tip: '-ul' makes this verb passive: 'konuşmak' is to speak, 'konuşulur' means is spoken.

target: Çocuklar hem alışveriş merkezinde gezdi hem de yeni kıyafetler aldı.
english: The children both wandered around the shopping mall and bought new clothes.
tip: 'hem ... hem de' links two facts as both and: 'hem gezdi hem de aldı' means both wandered and bought.

target: Kaptan yeni bir işletme kurmaya karar verdi.
english: The captain decided to start a new business.
tip: 'karar vermek' needs the '-maya' form of the next verb: 'kurmaya karar verdi' means decided to start.

target: Eczacı hafta içi konsere gidemeyecek kadar yoğundu.
english: The pharmacist was too busy during the week to go to the concert.
tip: 'gidemeyecek kadar yoğundu' means too busy to go: 'gidemeyecek' is cannot go and 'kadar' marks the degree, giving a too X to do reading.

target: Kütüphane caminin arkasında.
english: The library is behind the mosque.
tip: Position words like 'arkasında' (behind) mark the noun as the possessor: 'caminin arkasında' means at the back of the mosque.

target: Yarın geleceğini söyledi.
english: She said she would come tomorrow.
tip: For reported speech the verb takes '-eceğini': 'geleceğini' means that she would come, followed by 'söyledi' (said).

target: Bebek yeni yürümeyi öğrendi.
english: The baby has just learned to walk.
tip: Here 'yeni' means just or recently, not new: 'yeni yürümeyi öğrendi' means has just learned to walk.

target: Rüzgar esince eve koştum.
english: When the wind blew, I ran home.
tip: The suffix '-ince' means when or once something happens: 'esince' means when it blew.

target: Bu bina geçen yıl inşa edildi.
english: This building was built last year.
tip: Passive uses 'edildi' (was done) with a noun: 'inşa edildi' means was built, and no doer is named.

target: Her pazartesi ve çarşamba spor yapıyorum.
english: I exercise every Monday and Wednesday.
tip: Nouns pair with 'yapmak' (to do) to form verbs: 'spor yapıyorum' means I do sport, that is I exercise.

target: Bu benim çantam, seninkini gördün mü?
english: This is my bag, have you seen yours?
tip: Add '-ki' to make a possessive pronoun: 'seninki' means yours, and 'seninkini' adds the object ending '-ni'.

target: Yağmur yağarken evde kalmayı tercih ettim.
english: When it was raining, I preferred to stay home.
tip: The suffix '-ken' means while: 'yağarken' means while it was raining, marking two things happening at once.

target: Bu kitap ötekinden daha ilginç ve eğlenceli.
english: This book is more interesting and fun than the other one.
tip: Comparisons use '-den' plus 'daha': 'ötekinden daha ilginç' means more interesting than the other one.

target: Sabah sporunu yaptıktan sonra kendimi çok iyi hissediyorum.
english: I feel very good after doing morning exercise.
tip: For after doing something use '-tıktan sonra': 'yaptıktan sonra' means after doing it.

target: Bu kitap her yıl binlerce kişi tarafından okunur.
english: This book is read by thousands of people every year.
tip: To name the doer in a passive, use 'tarafından' (by): 'binlerce kişi tarafından' means by thousands of people.
